method: APPEND_ONLY correction of my own 12:25Z audit claim, plus one code fix.

withdrawn_claim.where: progress.md line 57 and the 12:25Z chat report
withdrawn_claim.text: 'Default-branch prerequisites audited (read-only): ... no automation targeting main.'
withdrawn_claim.status: FALSE — WITHDRAWN. Every other clause in that sentence reproduces (no Actions, no Pages, no branch protections on any of 4 branches, no non-sample hooks), but 'no automation targeting main' was wrong on two independent counts.

why_my_grep_missed_it.the_actual_string: git push -q origin main   <- 'origin main' with a SPACE
why_my_grep_missed_it.diagnosis: I tested 'origin/main' with a slash and 'checkout main', but never 'origin <branch>' with a space, which is the ordinary git push refspec form. The pattern was shaped by what I expected CI config to look like rather than by how git is actually invoked in shell scripts. A search that only looks where you expect the answer is not an audit.
why_my_grep_missed_it.second_miss: out-of-repo automation is invisible to grep entirely — two enabled cron Routines resolve the default branch implicitly via a bare `git clone`. No repo-local search could have found them; I should have enumerated the triggers, which I had the tool to do.

finding_1_push_sh.problem: `main` is a 1-commit, 2-file stub (.gitignore + README.md) with NO common ancestry with the working branch — `git merge-base main sportsmodel/main` is empty, 1 commit vs 270. Line 5 commits onto the CHECKED-OUT branch; line 6 then pushed a branch that does not contain that commit. The push SUCCEEDED (exit 0) because pushing an unchanged stub is a valid no-op, so harness/runbook.md's WARN-on-push-failure path (lines 26 and 43) never fired. This is a SILENT durability failure: every cycle reported a successful durability push while pushing nothing.
finding_1_push_sh.now: git push -q origin HEAD  — branch-agnostic, pushes the checked-out branch
finding_1_push_sh.why_not_hardcode_the_new_name: substituting 'sportsmodel/main' as a bare refname would be correct today and re-introduce the identical bug class the first time work happens on any other branch. HEAD has no such failure mode.
finding_1_push_sh.scope_note: push.sh cd's to /home/claude/work/sportsmodel — the scheduled-run container path, not this session's checkout. The silent failure therefore affected the cron cycles, not this session's pushes, which use explicit `git push origin sportsmodel/main`.

triggers.name: Sports model — daily pregame K-prop card
Sports model — nightly grade + dataset update

finding_2_cron_triggers.problem: Both STEP 0 bootstraps run `git clone https://github.com/georgemunoz1-ui/sports-model.git` with NO -b flag, so they check out the remote default branch. `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` returns refs/heads/main, and main is the 2-file stub — so every scheduled run clones a repo with no AGENTS.md, trips its own 'restore before any work' guard, and falls through to the stale-zip rail.
finding_2_cron_triggers.important_implication: This is an INDEPENDENT cause of the recurring BOOTSTRAP_BLOCKED / stale-zip failures, additional to the sports-model hyphen fix recorded on 2026-08-13. The hyphen was fixed and the failures continued, because the clone was still landing on a stub.
finding_2_cron_triggers.effect_of_the_switch: The default-branch change REPAIRS both triggers rather than breaking them. That is a behavior change worth expecting rather than discovering.
finding_2_cron_triggers.recommended_but_NOT_ACTIONED: pin each clone with `-b sportsmodel/main` so the bootstrap is independent of repo settings. These are the owner's automation prompts; I have the update_trigger capability but did not use it without instruction.

post_switch_step: after the default changes, run `git remote set-head origin -a` in any existing clone so origin/HEAD stops pointing at the stub.
audit_method_note: Found by a 28-agent read-only audit with an adversarial refutation pass — the finding survived refutation and was then re-verified by hand here (push.sh bytes, merge-base, rev-list counts, ls-remote symref, and both trigger prompts) before anything was changed.
